scope: Leakage-safe DROID wrist-to-exterior LoRA dataset build iterations v1-v9
summary: Nine immutable dataset iterations exposed blocked Git reads, absolute-path portability, missing holdouts, a too-short episode, an incorrect heldout count, and an unnecessarily large encoding before the accepted v10/v11 contracts were produced.
evidence: v1 stopped on a blocked Git subprocess; v5 stopped on a blocked .git/HEAD read.
v2 completed with absolute asset paths and v3 used relative paths but omitted heldout assets, so neither was accepted for remote training and evaluation.
v6 rejected episode 79 because it is too short for the fixed 17-frame, 8 FPS contract after earlier clips had already been emitted.
v7 built the full 91-episode joint target-A/target-B dataset but was larger than required for the requested target-A specialization.
v8 exposed an incorrect heldout-example count; v9 corrected the count but used CRF 16 and was superseded by the smaller CRF 24 contract.
Every failed or superseded directory is preserved; no earlier attempt was rewritten as successful.
lessons: Episode duration must be filtered before clip extraction begins.
Portable manifests require paths relative to the manifest directory and an explicit heldout asset contract.
Dataset specialization by target camera avoids doubling storage and optimizer steps when only one exterior view is being trained.
limitations: These iterations are engineering evidence, not model-quality evidence.
next_actions: Use only the accepted v10 or v11 contract for training and heldout evaluation.
